_doc: Policy identity lock. One id@version names exactly one content hash, forever: change a policy's content and you must raise its version and lock the new pair. Entries are never rewritten - old ones are how a stored run's hash stays traceable after the policy moves on.

policy_hash is the 64-hex SHA-256 over the None-free canonical IR. The top-level hash_scheme (sha256-canonical-v2) is the scheme of every entry that carries no hash_scheme of its own - all entries locked up to 2026-10-06; an entry locked since records its own hash_scheme. legacy_hashes are the 16-hex forms the same content carried under earlier code, so manifests written before 2026-10-06 still resolve: legacy16-exclude-none (runs up to 2026-08-31; it is also the first 16 hex of policy_hash), legacy16-valid-time (4950be1, 2026-09-01, a window of hours), legacy16-include-defaults (445bdbe 2026-09-01 to 2026-10-06).

hashes (optional, per entry) records the SAME content's hash under a later canonical scheme, added by lock --update and never replacing policy_hash. Scheme sha256-canonical-v3 (2026-10-06) stores WGS84 points as lat/lon instead of projected metres; it differs from v2 only for geographic policies (today wgs84_taipei.yaml), so only that entry carries one.
derived lists policies that exist only mid-flight (a hot-applied rule bumps generation and the hash), with the recipe to rebuild them.

ir_schema pins what every IR field means when omitted, under the IR schema version it was pinned at (ir_schema.version = guardrail.models.IR_SCHEMA_VERSION); see guardrail.models.ir_schema_defaults and tests/test_policy_hash.py. The freeze rule (2026-11-02, grant R6): ANY change to the pinned shape - a new field, even one defaulting to None, a new model, a changed default, a removal - needs a higher IR_SCHEMA_VERSION and a row in docs/IR-MIGRATIONS.md; lock --update then re-pins `defaults` and appends what changed to `migrations` (from, to, on, changes), so earlier pins can be read back. additive_pins records the two additions pinned WITHOUT a bump before that rule (2026-10-07 and 2026-10-19).
Maintain with: python -m guardrail.bundle lock [--update]. Checked by tests/test_policy_hash.py.

migrated_from (since 2026-11-02, IR schema 3.0.0): an entry locked because an IR change moved the policy's hash without changing its rules names the entry it migrates. The claim is re-proved by check_lock: the file's policy, put back at the old version, must reproduce the old entry's recorded hash under an IR 2.x form (guardrail.models.Policy.ir2_hashes) and its legacy hashes. policy_candidates offers that rewound policy, so runs flown under the old version still resolve. ir_schema_version on an entry names the IR schema it was locked under (absent: 2.x). Two later migrations are read back the same way, each by its own reading of the file (guardrail.bundle.rewind): the frame migration (2026-11-03, IR schema 3.1.0; old_hash_form sha256-canonical-v3/local-metres: the file's metre form, Policy.metre_form) and the scope migration (2026-11-06, IR schema 4.0.0; sha256-canonical-v3/ir-3.x: the file with every rule's scope left out, Policy.ir3_form).

migrations.why: WP1-01 / WP1-02 (2026-11-02): constraint_type, priority and violation_action are required on every rule (they defaulted to hard / P0 / repair); violation_action holds the grant's six only - `repair` is read as project_fix and never stored; polygon rings (polygon_fence, dynamic_nfz) are stored in canonical order (positive winding over the stored pairs, smallest pair first). Every shipped policy's hash moved, so each raised its patch version; its new entry names the old one in migrated_from, and check_lock re-proves that the old hash is reproduced (Policy.ir2_hashes).

XY.y: default '<required>' -> '<absent>'; every policy that omits it changes meaning
migrations.why: WP1-14 (2026-11-03): x / y are optional on a point, not required - a WGS84 point stores lat/lon only and its metres are a view computed when first read, from the frame origin its policy binds it to (models.XY, projection.local_metres). Every 3.0.0 document still validates; a required field made optional changes the meaning of no document that states it, and the canonical form held a WGS84 point as lat/lon only already, so no stored hash moved (all 32 policy files hash as under 3.0.0).

migrations.why: WP1-01 (2026-11-06): `scope` is required on every rule, as the grant's ConstraintBase writes it (it was absent by default, which meant "mission"). A field every writer must now give is a breaking change, hence the major version. A document of an earlier era - a bundle whose manifest names an older ir_schema_version, a lock recipe recorded before, a replay bundle or a run's policy_g<N>.json - is read in its own era (models.era_context): scope stays absent where it wrote none, so it hashes exactly as stored. Every shipped policy now states scope (mission on all 154 rules: every rule is a mission-layer rule), so each raised its patch version; its new entry names the old one in migrated_from with old_hash_form sha256-canonical-v3/ir-3.x, and check_lock re-proves that the file with scope left out (Policy.ir3_form) reproduces the old entry's hash and legacy hashes.

random-scenario@0.1.0.known_defect: 9 files with different content share this one policy_id and version, so `random-scenario@0.1.0` names no single policy. They are generated scenario policies (hard_*/hp_* and random_scenario.yaml). Each file is pinned below so a content change is still caught; the fix is a distinct policy_id per file, which changes their hashes and is left to whoever owns policies/*.yaml. Recorded 2026-10-06.
